Commentary.Commentary: That's it from this game! We have got the first team who are through to the finals, it's Australia. Which means the last game on Friday is a straight knockout between the hosts West Indies and South Africa. Who will join the mighty Aussies for the finale on Sunday? We shall find out soon. Until then, it's goodbye from us! Cheers!

MAN OF THE MATCH, MARLON SAMUELS says he is happy that his partnership with Ramdin worked out as they spoke about getting partnerships in their team meetings. Adds the next game on Friday is a very important one and he is looking forward to it. Hopes his purple patch continues for his team. Ends up saying he has some friends in the South African team and is up for the challenge on Friday.

Australian captain, STEVEN SMITH says that thinks that West Indies played very well today and they fought back from their earlier position. He felt the partnership between Marlon Samuels and Denesh Ramdin nearly pulled the match away from them but his team mates did a good job in pulling the match back. He says that his side generally has not been starting well with the ball but were successful this time. Unfortunately, their middle overs weren't as good but hopes that they play better on Sunday. He felt the target of 283 was a tough one but Mitchell Marsh played well and Maxwell with his trademark sweeps helped chase it down. He said he loves plays good, hard cricket and will continue to do so as long as they don't cross any lines and continue to win. He looks forward to playing whichever team wins in the upcoming match and is not bothered about whom his side will play in the finals.

West Indies skipper, JASON HOLDER says he was confident at the halfway mark. Adds the partnership between Samuels and Ramdin set the tone for them. Appreciates Samuels for the way he laid the foundation with a ton. On his injury, he says he strained his left hamstring and is hoping to be alright for the next game. Further says, Fletcher did well by bowling three tight overs but they were one bowler short and that cost them. Ends up saying South Africa are a tough opponent and they have to be at their very best to defeat them.

Debutant Gabriel was the pick of the Windies bowlers while Benn was tidy too. However, the other bowlers couldn't quite maintain the pressure on the Australians. Narine wasn't too expensive but he couldn't strike a single blow today. West Indies needed wickets at constant intervals but that didn't quite happen as the Australians cruised through in their run chase. Windies were also hampered by the absence of Holder who just bowled 2 overs before leaving the field with a hamstring injury. It was a wonderfully paced chase from Australia and they will go into the final high on confidence. Earlier in the afternoon, a masterclass ton from Samuels and a fine knock from Ramdin propelled WI to 282. In the end, it just wasn't enough.

A comfortable win for Australia in the end as they seal their berth in the final of the tri-series. Chasing a stiff target of 283, the openers got the Aussies off to a flier but both Finch and Khawaja departed in succession to put pressure on the World Champions. However, the pressure of a virtual knockout game brought out the best in skipper Smith who steadied things initially with Bailey. The skipper then along with Marsh put on 122 for the 4th wicket with the latter showing exemplary maturity after being promoted to number 5. Although Smith was run out in a mix up, Maxwell came in and launched a blitzkrieg to ensure that the game was finished with 8 balls to spare.

Welcome back for the run chase! Remember it's a must-win for the Aussies and they have to be right on the money if they are to qualify for the finals. AARON FINCH and USMAN KHAWAJA will open the batting for Australia. JASON HOLDER will steam in first up. Here we go!!!
